context.guidance: Serve every route that carries Personal Data over TLS only, and set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite attributes on session cookies. Replace wildcard cross-origin rules with an explicit list of trusted origins. These transport and session controls are part of the safeguards Rule 6(1)(a) requires for the Personal Data they carry.

value.fix: Replace `res.jsonp(response)` with `res.json(response)` so the personal data is not returned as a script-loadable JSONP payload, which is open to cross-origin JSONP hijacking. If JSONP must stay, allow only a strict allowlisted callback name (for example `/^[A-Za-z_$][\w$.]*$/`) and set `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Apply the SEC-11 controls at the app level: redirect HTTP to HTTPS and send HSTS for every route that carries personal data; set `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Strict` (or `Lax`) on all session cookies; and replace any wildcard CORS configuration (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` or `cors()` with no options) with an explicit list of trusted origins, checked against the request `Origin` header. Then verify with a test that a cross-origin request from an untrusted origin gets no CORS grant and no personal data, that session cookies carry all three attributes, and that plain-HTTP requests are redirected.
